questions.solution_text:
The shaded region runs from $x=2$ to $x=5$, so these are the lower and upper limits.
The height of the region at each $x$ is $3x-2$, so this is the integrand.
Area $=\int_{2}^{5}(3x-2)\,dx$

questions.solution_text:
Each strip has a boundary at its left end and at its right end, and neighbouring strips share a boundary.
So $n$ strips have $n+1$ boundary points.
Number of boundary points $=10+1$
$=11$

questions.solution_text:
In the sum, the rectangle height is $2x+5$ and the width is $\Delta x$.
The interval runs from $x=3$ to $x=8$.
$\lim_{\Delta x\to 0}\sum_{3}^{8}(2x+5)\,\Delta x$
$=\int_{3}^{8}(2x+5)\,dx$

For $0\le x\le 2$, the largest value of $x^{2}$ is $4$, so the largest value of $x^{2}-9$ is $-5$.
Every value of the integrand is negative, so every rectangle height $f(x)$ is negative.
The limit of the sum of these signed areas is negative.

questions.solution_text:
One rectangle has area $R\,\Delta t$, a rate in kilograms per second multiplied by a time in seconds.
That product is a mass in kilograms.
Adding all the rectangles estimates the total mass of grain added over the $20$ seconds, in kilograms.

questions.solution_text:
The number at the bottom of the integral sign is the lower limit, $-4$.
The number at the top is the upper limit, $1$.
The function between the integral sign and $dx$ is the integrand, $x+6$.

options.why: A sum over $n$ strips is only an estimate; without the limit as $n\to\infty$ it is not the exact area.
Uses the upper limit $b=10$ as the total width instead of $b-a=8$.
Divides the width by the number of boundary points, $n+1$, instead of the number of strips, $n$.

questions.solution_text:
The strip width is $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$
$=\frac{10-2}{n}$
$=\frac{8}{n}$
Each rectangle has area $\frac{20}{x}\cdot\frac{8}{n}$, so the estimate is $\sum_{2}^{10}\frac{20}{x}\cdot\frac{8}{n}$.
The estimate becomes exact only in the limit, giving $\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{2}^{10}\frac{20}{x}\cdot\frac{8}{n}$.
